gardenSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Cesar ODonnell. Beekeeper. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dog tags, Field suture kit, Trail compass, Grandma's Tin Cup, Hard Candy. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
"Hey." A woman, maybe 30s settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 30s.)
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
A person, maybe 50s, with a scarred cheek will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
🌱 A person, maybe 50s, with a scarred cheek looks over the garden: turned soil, nothing planted. Someone has to sow first.
Teresa is staying at Haven as the camp healer now — tending the sick instead of ranging out.

Journal: Open ground by water — the onion beds.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND Green Thumb, Literally. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.
★ IDENTIFIED: Wild Onion. Grass-like, smells like onion. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
★ IDENTIFIED: Dandelion. Jagged leaves, yellow flower. You grab the whole plant. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.

A man, maybe 60s, with a broad frame spends the afternoon with the thorny climbing vines everywhere, with tender coiled tips in spring — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
★ IDENTIFIED: Greenbrier Shoots. Greenbrier. Thorny vines, tender spring tips that snap like asparagus. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 The thorny climbing vines everywhere, with tender coiled tips in spring — THAT's what A man, maybe 60s, with a broad frame was describing. Greenbrier Shoots. It clicks like a key turning.
